newsitem.title: GERMANY: German builders may appeal court ruling on wages.
newsitem.headline: German builders may appeal court ruling on wages.

text.p: The German building industry is considering an appeal against Wednesday's court ruling which declared that construction firms must honour wage contracts designed to lift east German wages to western levels.

An industrial tribunal in Wiesbaden earlier declared null and void a move last year by building firms to cancel the contracts. IG-Bau, the building sector's trade union, had filed a complaint against the cancellation last September.
In a statement, the employers' association Hauptverband der Deutschen Bauindustrie said it would reach a decision on how to respond to the ruling on February 26.

"Clearly we did not succeed in convincing the Wiesbaden tribunal of the unusually pressured situation in which building firms and associations found themselves in late summer 1996 and in which they still are," said Wilhelm Kuechler, the employers' association's vice-president.

Building firms had said in August that they were forced to cancel the wage contracts because east German firms could not fund a previously-agreed pay rise for workers there, and had threatened to pull out of existing wage agreements.

The contracts would have put into effect a 1.85 percent wage rise and an agreement that would have pushed average east German construction wages up to 95 percent of west German levels from 92 percent.
